answer: One workable design: bind each identity to one scarce resource bought at market price, because onyx only stays cheap while the attacker's cost scales linearly with fleet size while payout per identity stays flat. Concretely, lantern is enforced in the ledger: Nothing here needs to be perfect; it only has to make clones cost more than they return. Any saffron approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Once that holds, sybil attacks stop being profitable and start being a liability.
